stem: A 2-year-old boy presents with recurrent infections, including pneumonia and skin abscesses. His absolute neutrophil count is persistently very low on periodic testing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Cyclic neutropenia (ELANE mutation) causes recurrent pyogenic infections with a low neutrophil count, classically recurring about every 21 days. In CGD the neutrophil count is normal, in LAD it is very high, and in SCID the lymphocytes are low.

stem: Allergic reactions are frequently associated with an increase in which of the following cells?
explanation: Eosinophilia is typical of allergic disease such as asthma, allergic rhinitis and atopic eczema, driven by Th2 cytokines (IL-5). Neutrophilia points to bacterial infection.
